title: rulekit rule set
description: One trial's eligibility criteria as code. Normative definition of the format is FORMAT.md; this schema is the machine-checkable half of it. Constraints this file cannot express are listed in FORMAT.md under 'What the schema cannot check'.

ruleset.description: Stable identifier for the rule set. Does not change across versions.

rulesetVersion.description: Semantic version of this rule set. MAJOR = a criterion was removed or its meaning inverted; MINOR = a criterion was added or a threshold moved; PATCH = wording/provenance only, no behavioural change.

factModel.description: Name of the fact model every `fact` reference is resolved against, e.g. `patient-facts/v1`.

protocol.description: Sponsor's protocol identifier and version, as printed on the protocol document.

status.description: Free text lifecycle label (`draft`, `irb-approved`, `completed`). Not interpreted by the engine.

effective.description: ISO-8601 date this version became effective at the site.

source.description: Where the criteria text came from.

id.description: Unique within the rule set, kebab-case. Appears in traces, coverage reports and behavioural diffs, so renaming one is a breaking change to every downstream artifact.

ref.description: The criterion's position in the source protocol (`I1`, `E4`, `AGE`). Free text — the protocol's numbering, not ours.

kind.description: inclusion: the condition must be true for the patient to qualify. exclusion: the condition being true disqualifies the patient.

verbatim.description: The criterion exactly as written in the protocol. Required even when `unmodeled`, and never edited to fit the language.

unmodeled.description: This criterion cannot be expressed in the condition language. It is carried as verbatim text and always evaluates `unknown`, which pushes affected patients to `undetermined` rather than silently passing them.

condition.description: A closed condition language: three combinators over four families of leaf. Deliberately not a general expression language — the closed set is what makes static interval analysis and the threshold slider tractable.

numericLeaf.description: Compare a `number` fact against a literal. A missing fact evaluates `unknown`; a present but non-numeric value also evaluates `unknown` (never a silent false).

unit.description: The unit the literal is written in. No conversion is performed: a unit that differs from the fact model's declaration raises the `unit-mismatch` warning and the values are still compared as-is.

setLeaf.description: Membership of a `code` fact in an inline value set. `in` is true when any entry matches; `notIn` is its exact negation.

existsLeaf.description: Presence of the fact in the patient record. The one leaf that never returns `unknown` — absence is the answer, not a gap. See FORMAT.md: `exists` cannot distinguish 'never measured' from 'measured and quarantined'.

withinLeaf.description: The single temporal operator: a code-set match on a `code` fact whose entry carries `daysAgo <= windowDays`. A matching entry with no date evaluates `unknown` — an undated med is not evidence of a washout.

codeRef.description: An inline value set. No terminology server: the codes a criterion needs are written into the criterion, so the rule set is self-contained and diffable.

system.description: Must be one of the systems the fact model declares for this fact (`snomed`, `rxnorm`, `rxnorm-class`, ...).

factName.description: A fact declared by the rule set's `factModel`. An undeclared name is the `unknown-fact` error.
